what_happened: All three method lessons named by the dispatch were authored directly in the source store with no ambiguity about target file/location; the dispatch's own Description already named exact filenames, section targets, and measured detail, so no additional research or disambiguation was needed.

The research dispatch authored all three method lessons in the source store rather than only researching them, so the plan phase found the content already complete and verified; the plan was rescoped from authoring to registration, cross-linking, lint cleanup and verification.

validate-artifact.sh caught a false __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel claim in a phase Tier Justification: index-entries.json maps to five real suites. A combined multi-path suite_selection_select call had masked this; per-path re-measurement fixed the justification before the plan was finalized.

Phase 1's gate-3,4 verification subset (source-store check-extension-docs.sh) showed two findings after Phase 1's own edits: (1) lean/index-entries.json line_count drift for dependency-tracing.md (229 declared vs 237 actual) -- EXPECTED, the plan's own Phase 2 task explicitly refreshes this; (2) Rule S deployed-index-orphan for the new pattern file -- this checks the DEPLOYED .claude/context/index.json directly, which only syncs from source index-entries.json at redeploy time; since redeploy is an explicit Non-Goal of this plan, this finding cannot be resolved within this task's scope and will persist through Phase 3's full gate run as well.

All three method lessons authored by the prior research-round dispatch were verified fully content-complete on first inspection across all three phases -- no re-authoring, no content gaps, no divergence from the dispatch's stated requirements. The plan's own scope hypotheses (43 entries/no duplicate, one 'no longer' occurrence, no existing See Also section, exactly one garbled Decisions bullet) were all confirmed exactly as predicted, letting every phase proceed without re-planning.
